newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal militants gun down 18 in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal militants gun down 18 in northeast India.

text.p: Separatist tribal guerrillas on Tuesday ambushed two vehicles of security personnel and shot dead 18 people in India's remote northeastern state of Tripura, police said.
The incident took place at Chamanu in Dhalai district, about 180 km (120 miles) north of state capital Agartala.
Vibhuti Chakravarty, a senior police official, told Reuters in Agartala the guerrillas opened fire from a hill-top, killing most of them on the spot. Ten people were also wounded.

"Eighteen security personnel of the territorial army and General Reserve Engineering Force, attatched to the army, were gunned down by the suspected National Liberation Front of Tripura militants this morning," Chakravarty said.
The wounded were admitted to hospital in Agartala and the condition of six of them was serious, hospital officials said.
The state government has asked the army and paramilitary forces to carry out search operations to track down the suspected militants.
"The government will not spare anyone responsible for the killings," state interior minister Samar Chaudhury said.
Chaudhury said the state had asked for the federal government's assistance in combating terrorism in Tripura.
The National Liberation Front of Tripura is an outlawed guerrilla outfit that has been fighting for a separate homeland since 1989.
A number of separatist groups, some tribal and others with Maoist ideologies, operate in the region's seven hilly states and accuse New Delhi of ignoring the area's economy.
In February, a different group of tribal guerrillas, the All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF), killed at least 50 people in west Tripura, setting houses ablaze and leaving thousands homeless.

The federal government then granted sweeping shoot-at-sight powers to soldiers deployed in the thickly wooded state and authorised army and paramilitary reinforcements to arrest and indefinitely detain suspects.
